comment: Pivot-test MEMORY sweep policy (imported by prod.json / suffix.json INSTEAD of pivot-scoped-sweeps.json when you want the solidcommunity.net behavior). Disposable session state (cookies, transient OIDC adapter state) lives in MemoryMapStorage - a restart logs users out but avoids high-frequency disk writes and their lock churn. State that must survive restarts (OIDC client registrations, forgot-password and ownership tokens) stays persisted with sweeps scoped to their own subtree via ContainerPathStorage + MaxKeyLengthStorage over ScopedJsonResourceStorage - no full /.internal/ tree walk, key hashing and on-disk layout unchanged. Memory storages keep ContainerPathStorage so the key space is identical to the disk layout. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with pivot-scoped-sweeps.json: import exactly ONE of the two (both override CookieStorage and IdpAdapterExpiringStorage).

@graph.comment: Keep session cookies in memory (a restart requires users to log in again) - avoids high-frequency cookie writes to disk and their lock churn.
Scope the forgot-password sweep to its own container (persisted - mailed links must survive restarts).
Scope the ownership-token sweep to its own container (persisted).
Keep transient OIDC grants/sessions/tokens/replay state in memory (fork-native @id) - short-lived by design, nothing of value survives a restart; eliminates adapter disk writes and sweep load.

Scope the persistent OIDC client-registration sweep to its own container (fork-native @id, persisted). Client keys are long and hashed, so ContainerPathStorage + MaxKeyLengthStorage must be preserved for on-disk compatibility.
